task.description:
CODE-DESIGNER pass (WF-02 Step 1) for REQ-167 (queue task 319, GH#619). Read REQ-167's full entry in docs/requirements.yaml (id: REQ-167) before anything else -- it is long and precise, read it in full, do not work from this summary alone. Produce a design artefact under lib/letflow/design/ (e.g. req167-wasm-import-whitelist.md) per this project's CODE-DESIGNER conventions (see req166-wasm-module-abi-validation.md and req165-wasmex-process-boundary.md as recent examples of the expected depth/rigor -- both went through real rework rounds driven by independently-reproduced findings, not rubber-stamped). Design only -- zero implementation code, @spec/@type/interface-level content only.

Core substance: WASM-06 (import whitelist) requires that the Wasmtime instance's import table be built FROM the module manifest's declared capabilities (a whitelist, not a denylist -- an unnamed host function must be absent, not merely unreachable), and that instantiation FAILS (not a present-but-erroring import) when a module imports anything outside that whitelist. WASM-07 (no filesystem access by default) is being restated here exactly as REQ-166 restated req163's instantiation-rejection assignment: the literal acceptance-criterion string 'wasi:filesystem/types' is a WASI Preview 2 COMPONENT-MODEL interface name, and REQ-163 chose CORE MODULES (see req163-wasm-abi-choice.md) -- so asserting that literal name against a core-module runtime would be a false pass (rejected as unrecognised regardless of any real filesystem policy). Your design must identify REQ-163's artefact's named concrete import surface to assert denial against instead (read req163-wasm-abi-choice.md section 4 and any other section naming this surface -- it names the exact surface REQ-166 already exercised, e.g. wasi_snapshot_preview1 namespace imports, as prior art), and the moduledoc plan must state explicitly: (a) that WASM-07's literal name is not the surface tested, (b) what IS tested instead and why asserting the literal name would be a false pass under core modules, (c) whether any explicit filesystem-grant path exists today (if none, say so plainly rather than imply the requirement's 'future grant MUST be explicit in the capability manifest' clause is implemented).

Think carefully about WHERE this whitelist-building logic lives relative to Letflow.Engine.Wasm.ModuleRegistry (REQ-166, registration-time ABI validation) and Letflow.Engine.Wasm.PluginHandler (REQ-165, invocation/process-boundary) -- this is a THIRD, distinct concern (authorization/capability enforcement at instantiation time, driven by a manifest that neither REQ-165 nor REQ-166 consume), so decide and justify explicitly whether it is a new module, an extension of one of the existing two, or something else, following this repo's own separation-of-concerns precedent (req155-lua-wallclock-kill.md section 4.4, already cited in req166's own design). Also decide explicitly how the 'module manifest' referenced by WASM-06/07 is represented at this point in the system -- check whether a manifest schema/type already exists anywhere in lib/letflow/ (grep for 'manifest' in lib/letflow/engine/) before inventing a new one; if none exists yet, define the minimal shape this requirement needs (e.g. a capability list) rather than a speculative full schema, and flag that a fuller manifest format is presumably a separate/future requirement's concern if that's genuinely true.

CRITICAL METHODOLOGY NOTE (from repeated findings this pipeline has made on WASM designs): if you make any claim about wasmex's live behavior (e.g. what happens when Wasmex.start_link/1 is given a WASI-less Store but the module still declares certain imports; what Wasmex.Module.imports/1 or similar introspection returns; whether an import table can be selectively populated with only some host functions), you MUST actually verify it with a real MIX_ENV=test mix run script against the installed dependency (WASMEX_BUILD=true, export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH") before writing it into the design -- do not assert it from documentation or plausible-sounding inference. Two of REQ-166's design defects were exactly this failure mode (a misread citation and a false unverified live-behavior claim), both caught by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own independent reproduction. Read deps/wasmex/lib/wasmex.ex and deps/wasmex/lib/wasmex/module.ex directly for the real API surface (start_link's imports option, how a WASI-less instance's import table is actually built and whether partial/selective host-function grants are even representable in the current wasmex version) rather than assuming.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: a test asserts a module declaring only var:read and importing the service-call host function FAILS TO INSTANTIATE (WASM-06's own acceptance criterion) -- design must specify exactly what error shape this produces and where it's raised (mirroring REQ-166's {:error, {:instantiation_failed, ...}} shape where reasonable, or justifying a divergence).

AC2: a test asserts the import table is built from the manifest as a whitelist -- a host function not named by the manifest is ABSENT from the instance's imports, asserted by INSPECTING the instance (not by invoking and catching an error). Design must specify a concrete, verified (per the methodology note above) mechanism for this inspection given wasmex's real API.
AC3: a test asserts a module attempting filesystem access under REQ-163's chosen ABI is rejected, using the concrete import surface REQ-163's artefact names (not the literal 'wasi:filesystem/types').
AC4: the moduledoc states that WASM-07's literal name is NOT the surface tested, names what IS tested instead, and explains why the literal name would be a false pass under core modules.
AC5: the moduledoc explicitly restates WASM-07 (intent implemented, concrete name ABI-dependent and replaced per REQ-163) the same way REQ-166's moduledoc restated req163's assignment.
AC6: the moduledoc states plainly whether an explicit filesystem-grant path exists today; if none, says so rather than implying the 'future grant' clause is implemented.

AC7 (from the requirement's own scope note): design states explicitly where the whitelist-building logic lives (new module vs. extending ModuleRegistry/PluginHandler) and why, with an explicit manifest-representation decision.
Zero literal Elixir code in the design doc -- @spec/@type/interface descriptions only.
Full traceability table mapping every one of REQ-167's real acceptance criteria (read from docs/requirements.yaml, there may be more than the 7 numbered above -- use the real ones) to a planned test.

result.summary: Design artefact lib/letflow/design/req167-wasm-import-whitelist.md and test/specs/REQ-167.md written. Decision: new module Letflow.Engine.Wasm.CapabilityGate (plus new Letflow.Engine.Wasm.CapabilityGateTaskSupervisor), fully decoupled from ModuleRegistry (REQ-166) and PluginHandler (REQ-165) -- a third, distinct concern (manifest-driven import-table construction + gated instantiation), per req155 sec4.4 / req166 sec2.2 precedent. Manifest represented as a minimal inline type (@type manifest :: %{capabilities: [String.t()]}), not a new top-level module or a port of Lua.Manifest's hash/script-id machinery -- vocabulary matches Letflow.Engine.Lua.Capabilities's opaque-string, exact-match-only tokens without a hard code dependency between the two subsystems. All wasmex live-behavior claims (imports: option is a real selective host-function grant with no implicit universal grant underneath it; an ungranted import crashes with the identical {{:badmatch, {:error, message}}, stacktrace} shape req166 already reproduced, regardless of namespace; an unused whitelist entry is inert; no wasmex API exposes a running instance's resolved import table, so AC2's 'inspect the instance' assertion necessarily targets build_import_table/1's pure return value) were verified via a real MIX_ENV=test mix run script against the installed wasmex v0.15.1 dependency (WASMEX_BUILD=true), not inferred from docs -- see design sec1. WASM-07 restated per req163 sec4's named wasi_snapshot_preview1/path_open surface, with the moduledoc content plan explicitly covering: (a) wasi:filesystem/types is not the surface tested, (b) what is tested instead and why the literal name would be a false pass under core modules, (c) that no explicit filesystem-grant path exists today. Full traceability table (design sec9) maps all 7 real REQ-167 acceptance criteria from docs/requirements.yaml to design elements and to test/specs/REQ-167.md's T1-T6. Zero implementation code in either artefact -- @spec/@type/@doc and prose/tables only. mix letflow.lint_handoffs run clean. No file under lib/letflow/engine/wasm/ (module_registry.ex, plugin_handler.ex) modified; nothing pushed, merged, or implemented.
